Flag tokens whose f0 has gaps inside the measured region

Source: R/resample.R
flag_f0_gaps.Rd

Adds two token-level columns so unvoiced stretches are visible in the exported data rather than being silently scattered NAs: n_missing, the number of that token's rows with no f0, and has_gap, TRUE when the token's voicing is interrupted somewhere between its first and last f0.

Usage

flag_f0_gaps(df, token = "token", f0 = "f0", time = "time", run = "voiced_run")

Arguments

df

Long-format f0 data frame.

token, f0, time

Column names. Defaults "token", "f0", "time". Without the time column, rows are taken in their order in df and only rows without f0 mark a gap.

run

Name of a column that numbers the runs of f0 within each token, such as voiced_run. Used only when the column is present; NULL ignores it.

Value

df with the n_missing and has_gap columns added. Columns of these names already in df are replaced, keeping their values for the tokens with no rows without f0 (see Details).

Details

The distinction matters because a missing value at the edge of a region usually just means the region ran slightly past the voicing, while a missing value in the middle means voicing was interrupted (a medial voiceless stop, a creaky patch, or a tracking failure). Only the latter sets has_gap, so has_gap marks the tokens worth looking at in F0 Correction. Run this on the native frames rather than on a resampled grid: resampling can fill a short dropout from its nearer frame, leaving no NA behind for this to find, and its equal time steps show no gap either.

A gap is one of these:

  • rows without f0 between two rows with f0;

  • a time step longer than 1.5 times the token's usual step, so the gaps still show once the rows without f0 are removed. This needs a regular frame grid and a time column;

  • a change in the run column (voiced_run), when the data have one.

Once the rows without f0 are removed, n_missing can no longer count them. So for a token with no rows without f0, the values the data already hold in n_missing and has_gap are kept, as they may record rows removed earlier. has_gap is also set to TRUE there when the token has a gap (above). Other tokens get both columns afresh. On data cleaned beforehand that hold neither column and no run column, on a grid that is not regular, no gap can be seen: such a token gets n_missing = 0 and has_gap = FALSE.

A token with no f0 at all gets has_gap = FALSE: there is no interior to speak of.

See also

resample_f0_equal(), trim_to_voiced(); screen_f0_rows() for the gaps counted per token without changing the data.
